# Overview {#overview}

## Two packages, one bundle format {-}

scMINER Viewer is intentionally split into two co-equal packages so
that:

* the **R** package owns data preparation (writing the bundle + graph
  layout) plus a Shiny single-study viewer and the multi-study
  browser;
* the **Python** package owns a Shiny-for-Python viewer + multi-study
  browser that consumes the same `.scminer.h5` bundle.

The shared contract is a single HDF5 file — `<studyID>.scminer.h5` —
written by R and read by either package. Every other feature lives on
top of this contract.

## Design decisions (locked) {-}

| Question | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Backend | Standalone, file-based | No Java services, no graph DB, no MySQL. Drop a study tree on disk and either package can render it. |
| Storage | HDF5 bundle alongside the graph-import shard tree | One file the apps load in one shot; preserves compatibility with the original Neo4j-import pipeline. |
| Lazy values | Bundle stores **indexes only** (which genes have shards); matrix values stay on disk | Bundles stay ~80 MB even when matrices are hundreds of MB. The app reads exactly one shard per gene-selection event. |
| Multi-study | One subfolder per study under a shared root | `prepare_study()` writes to `<root>/<studyID>/...`; `run_browser(root)` discovers every study. |
| UI tabs | Six core panels (Cluster / Heatmap / Bubble / Feature / Violin / Network) with nested per-gene → per-cell-type → per-relationship pickers | Mirrors the layout at <https://scminer.stjude.org/study/Tregs>. |
| Python UI framework | Shiny for Python | Same reactive model as R Shiny; minimises divergence between the two packages. |

## What's in scope {-}

* Reading scMINER ExpressionSet RDS / activity RDS / networks TSV via
  `prepare_study()` (R).
* Writing the graph-import layout (the existing Neo4j-style TSV +
  per-gene CSV tree).
* Writing the lazy-mode `.scminer.h5` bundle.
* Browsing one study at a time via `run_app()` (R) or
  `scminer-viewer run` (Python).
* Browsing many studies under a root via `run_browser()` (R) or
  `scminer-viewer browse` (Python).
* Cluster table with **checkbox** selection, color swatches, and
  live-updating per-cluster cell counts that respond to the Sampling %
  control.
* Downsampling (`Sampling %`) — auto-applied above 65K cells.
* Default-gene auto-load on app startup (mirrors the Vue portal's
  `preGenes`).
* Heatmap diverging blue-white-red palette.
* 3-level nested viewer tabs (Gene → CellType → Expression/TF/SIG)
  for the Feature, Violin, and Network panels.

## Repository layout {-}

```
scMINER-Viewer/
├── IMPLEMENTATION.md             architecture & status doc
├── README.md                     top-level entry point
├── book/                         this guide (bookdown)
├── data/                         multi-study root
│   └── 2327/
│       ├── 2327.scminer.h5
│       ├── Cell/, Gene/, Network_*/
│       ├── study_meta/, study_gene_*/
│       ├── expression_files/2327/
│       └── activity_files/2327/
├── scminerViewer/                R package
│   ├── R/, tests/
│   ├── inst/extdata/example_config.yml
│   └── inst/scripts/build_2327_bundle.R
└── scminer_viewer/               Python package
    └── src/scminer_viewer/{data,app,browser,cli}.py + plots/
```
